facts.text: I received an email from Dan Kennedy, who usually does not do email.
Dan Kennedy mentioned a recap at Russell Brunson's FHL event.
I think Dan Kennedy is right that most copywriters do not know or teach anything.
I believe most information can be found elsewhere for a better price or for free.
I believe a customer or subscriber could know everything (or believe they do) in a short amount of time.
I believe fiction writers should study non-fiction.
I believe non-fiction writers should read fiction.
I believe fiction writers should read news articles themselves, scan articles from various sources, pay attention to headlines, and study people’s daily habits and routines.
I believe writers should take in nature and look around even if it is boring or sucks.
I believe writers should make a movie out of the mundane.
I believe the same idea applies to non-fiction writers, including myself.
I believe I and many others who write ad copy and magazine/trade journal content should read as many fiction novels and fantasy books as possible.
I think adult cartoons today are better than kid cartoons, which I find tacky, boring, and unpalatable.
I mentioned South Park, Family Guy, The Simpsons, and Rick and Morty as adult animated shows that use real-life or relatable characters.
I said Marvel used characters like Spider-Man and Captain America.
I said the characters in those shows were built on trigger points seen in the media and in real life.
I said Dan Kennedy brought up Gary Halbert and Napoleon Hill in the email.
I said Dan Kennedy is still active in his and my world.
I said Napoleon Hill’s “Laws of Success” book includes something about Organized Effort.
I suggested Organized Effort might also be mentioned in “Think and Grow Rich,” but I said I could be wrong.
I said Dan Kennedy’s point was about writing by objectives.
I said writing by objectives is because writing persuades others, creates a sphere of influence, and forms long-term business relationships.
I said there should be a mission and not just writing without purpose.
I said free writing for fun and practice is totally fine and mandatory for learning and growth.
I said for 95% of writing, it should be intentional.
I said I believe there are no rewards in this game.
I said we can pat ourselves on the back sometimes but should forget what friends and family think.
I said friends and family will either shut down the idea or give a pat on the back routine.
I said it is all about results that take place in the marketplace.
I said it is difficult to know whether writing is good or not if you cannot figure out what you want to happen after the reader consumes the content.
I said writers can use story telling as a trick of the trade.
I said Gary Halbert used story telling a lot.
I said Gary Halbert’s newsletters were mostly pure story telling.
I said story telling was 90% of Gary Halbert’s content, according to my belief.
I said Dan Kennedy mentioned that if you went through a pile of Gary Halbert’s letters, you would find some teaching content scattered throughout.
I said most of Gary Halbert’s work was like a journal of his own life, daily rituals, and business dealings.
I compared Gary Halbert’s letters to daytime television or an episode of “Gary” in printed form.
I said Gary Halbert was known to be raw and honest.
I said when Gary Halbert’s letters arrived in subscribers’ mailboxes, recipients would barricade themselves and stop what they were doing to read the letters.
I said Gary Halbert’s letters were like soap operas.
I said I do not get paid or have anything to offer people for reading what I wrote.
I said it is helpful to me if people follow me here.
I signed the message as Justin N. McDonald.
I referred to the writing as being written this morning on the 22nd day of September.

events.text: I received an email from Dan Kennedy that included a recap of Russell Brunson's FHL event.
I wrote that the content was written this morning on the 22nd day of September.
